messages:
lina-acme: Hey team — onboarding is hitting 401s followed by 429s during SDK init. We spin up ~30 parallel workers for warmup and see auth failures then rate limits. Anyone seen this pattern?

marisa-cs: Thanks for the report. Can you paste the client-side init span and a short snippet of the error logs? Also what SDK (lang + version) are you using?

lina-acme: Using browser JS SDK v0.9.1. Quick log excerpt: 
```
[2024-08-01T12:34:10Z] auth: token_exchange ok
[2024-08-01T12:34:10Z] request /v1/generate 401 auth_error: invalid_token
[2024-08-01T12:34:11Z] request /v1/generate 429 rate_limit exceeded
[2024-08-01T12:34:11Z] retrying (0.1s)
[2024-08-01T12:34:11Z] request /v1/generate 429
```
We also see the same token used by many concurrent sockets.

devon-eng: Quick hypothesis: looks like a token race + short TTL + preflight fanout causing transient 401s which then push your traffic into a rate window. Two things to check: clock skew on clients and whether the ephemeral token refresh is being called for every worker instead of sharing a single token.

marisa-cs: Actionable checklist:
- Confirm token lifetime returned by our auth endpoint (exp claim).
- Ensure clients reuse token across workers for the warmup phase.
- If you must parallelize, stagger refreshes with jitter.
- Send a sample HTTP header dump (Authorization, x-client-id, x-region) — redact secrets.

lina-acme: Token TTL is 30s (short, we inherited this from a sidecar setup). Headers (redacted):
```
Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED]
x-client-id: acme-web
x-region: us-west-2
```

sam-edge: Also check for proxy rewriting issues — our edge sometimes strips `Authorization` for certain preflight routes. Can you run one request directly to origin (bypass edge) and one via edge to compare?

lina-acme: Ok running direct vs edge now... direct returns 200 consistently; via edge we get the 401/429 wave.

marisa-cs: That nails it — edge rewrite + short TTL + heavy concurrency = stampede. Short-term mitigation: reduce parallel warmup to ~4 concurrent workers and add exponential backoff with random jitter (0-200ms). Long-term: increase token TTL or use a shared refresh token flow.

devon-eng: If you want a quick server-side patch, we can add a small token-grace window on validation (+2s) to account for skew and immediate reuse. Not ideal for prod, but helpful for onboarding traffic patterns.

lina-acme: Will try the reduce-parallel approach and request edge team to check header passthrough. Thanks — any snippet for the jittered retry?

marisa-cs: Sample JS backoff snippet: 
```js
// simple jittered backoff for warmup
const base = 50; // ms
function jitterBackoff(attempt){
  return base * Math.pow(2, attempt) + Math.floor(Math.random()*200);
}
// use max 5 attempts per warmup request and cap concurrency at 4
```

lina-acme: Implemented cap to 4 and jitter, running warmup again. Early results: much fewer 401s and no 429 spike.

onboard-bot: Deploy note — created ticket CS-4921 for follow-up with edge-team and ENG-5023 for token TTL options.

marisa-cs: Great. I'll own coordination with edge team; devon will follow up on the token-grace PR. Reopen thread if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
